html:
SMTO-EXE-0114 — The web page took too long to load

GUID: fa03d893-f223-5271-8f5b-029e3a7f3828
Slug: browser-navigation-timeout
Domain: EXE · Subsystem: browser

What happened

  • SMTO stopped waiting for a page to finish loading. The website may still have received the request and changed something, so the browser could be on a new page.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Ask SMTO: "Which page is your browser showing now?" Don't ask it to load the page again yet. The page may have finished loading just after SMTO stopped waiting.
  2. If the step could have sent a form, such as a reload after pressing Submit, check on the website whether it already went through. Loading that kind of page again could send the same form twice.
  3. If the site is just slow, ask SMTO to open the page again and wait longer, up to one minute. SMTO waits about 10 seconds by default and can be asked to wait up to 60 seconds.
  4. If every site is slow, make sure the computer running the Gateway has a working internet connection. Pages load on the Gateway's computer, so its connection decides how fast they open.

What success looks like

  • SMTO reports that the intended page is loaded, and you've confirmed nothing was sent twice.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the web address, to the person who manages the Gateway. Don't keep repeating a reload that might submit a form or payment again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • A navigate, back, forward or reload operation on the Gateway hit its time limit (timeout_ms, default 10 s, at most 60 s) before the page finished loading; the request may already have reached the site.

What this means

  • Navigation reached the operation deadline or raised the recognized TimeoutError class; navigation may already have sent a request or changed the page. The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.

Why this can happen

  • Navigation reached the operation deadline or raised the recognized TimeoutError class; navigation may already have sent a request or changed the page.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the same tab's current URL/state and effect-unknown flag before another navigation.

How to fix it

  • BrowserService._execute raised navigation_timeout when the operation deadline passed or Playwright raised TimeoutError; effect_unknown reflects whether navigation was dispatched. Inspect browser.page_info before any further navigation, confirm the Gateway host can reach the site, and if appropriate repeat with a larger timeout_ms (maximum 60000).
  • Inspect browser.page_info before another navigation; the destination request may already have executed.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect browser.page_info before another navigation; the destination request may already have executed.

How to verify the fix

  • The original navigation is reconciled or safely left reported as uncertain before new action.

What not to do

  • Do not replay uncertain mutations, scan CDP endpoints, or export cookies/passwords/storage.

Technical notes

  • The retained effect boundary and original session identity govern recovery. Browser page content remains untrusted, diagnostic rendering adds no navigation or model call, and mutations are not automatically replayed.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
